description: This bar chart illustrates the number of samples used for different reasoning categories. The horizontal axis displays the categories: Mathematical Reasoning, General Reasoning, Natural Scene Reasoning, Physical Reasoning, Logical Puzzle Reasoning, and Chemical Reasoning, listed in order from largest to smallest bar height. The vertical axis is labeled “Number of Samples” and uses a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10<sup>2</sup> to 10<sup>4</sup>, with tick labels at intervals of 10<sup>2</sup>. There are six light blue bars, each corresponding to a reasoning category; the tallest bar represents “Mathematical Reasoning” with a value of 7025, while the shortest bar represents “Chemical Reasoning” with a value of 49. The bar for “General Reasoning” reaches a value of 1709, “Natural Scene Reasoning” reaches 413, “Physical Reasoning” reaches 232, and “Logical Puzzle Reasoning” reaches 91. No bars are visually emphasized or annotated.
